name: Baseline Defenses: Perplexity Filtering, Paraphrasing, and Adversarial Training
executive_summary: Three simple, model-agnostic defenses — perplexity-based detection, input paraphrase/retokenization, and adversarial training — evaluated as baselines against optimization-based jailbreaks.
description: Systematically evaluates three defense families borrowed from the broader adversarial-ML literature against LLM jailbreaks: detection via perplexity filtering (optimized adversarial suffixes tend to be low-fluency, high-perplexity token sequences that stand out from natural text), input preprocessing (paraphrasing or retokenizing the input to disrupt an attack's precise token sequence before the model sees it), and adversarial training (training directly against known attacks, at a documented quality/robustness tradeoff cost). Perplexity filtering and paraphrasing performed better than the adversarial-ML literature on other domains (e.g. vision) would predict, making them a comparatively cheap first line of defense to consider alongside the structural/privilege-based defenses elsewhere in this category.
when_to_use: Adding a lightweight, model-agnostic filtering layer in front of a system, particularly against optimization-based (GCG-style) attacks with distinctively low-fluency text.
when_not_to_use: Against fluency-constrained or hand-crafted attacks specifically designed to evade perplexity detection — this family of defenses is not a complete solution on its own.
known_pitfalls: Adversarial training's robustness gains come with a documented, sometimes severe, generation-quality cost — the paper found one training variant essentially useless because quality degraded far more than robustness improved.

primary_source.authors: Jain, Schwarzschild, Wen, Somepalli, Kirchenbauer, Chiang, Goldblum, Saha, Geiping, Goldstein
primary_source.title: Baseline Defenses for Adversarial Attacks Against Aligned Language Models

usage_templates.template: Compute the perplexity of the incoming input {{raw_input}} under a reference language model. If perplexity exceeds {{perplexity_threshold}} (calibrated on natural-language traffic), flag for review or reject rather than passing to the main model. Otherwise, optionally paraphrase {{raw_input}} into {{paraphrased_input}} before further processing, to disrupt any precise adversarial token sequence that survived the perplexity check.

variables.name: perplexity_threshold
variables.description: Cutoff above which input is flagged/rejected

variables.name: paraphrased_input
variables.description: The input after optional paraphrase/retokenize preprocessing

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
